text.p: Shares in Rhone-Poulenc rose strongly on Friday on the back of an investors' presentation by managing director Igor Landau to a lunch organised by brokers Exane, fund managers said.
"The company has made a very positive presentation for investors," said a fund manager. Rhone-Poulenc said no new information was given since its January 30 annual results presentation.

According to fund managers, Landau said that Rhone-Poulenc's share was cheap because it was valued like a chemical stock while it is more a drugs stock with 70 percent of its profits coming from its pharmaceutical activities.
He also said that the group would not engage in any alliance with another pharmaceutical group as long as its price/earnings ratio, of about 12, was not equal to other drugs groups at 20.
He also said that the group would do everything to increase shareholders' value by concentrating on its strong points.

At chemicals, where 34 billion francs in sales generate two percent of profits. "the policy is quite clear -- or it generates lots of cash after the restructuring, or it will be sold," a fund manager said.
At 1133 GMT, Rhone was up 2.89 percent at 192 francs while the blue-chip index was up 0.38 percent at 2,638.61.
